business_problem: IBM product teams were receiving tens of thousands of feature requests, categorizing many of them manually, and using inconsistent local tools that made prioritization slow, duplicative, and hard to compare across products.
solution_summary: The IBM Chief Analytics Office piloted a watsonx.ai-based prioritization workflow to help product managers process feature ideas across IBM teams. Instead of relying on an optional user-entered theme field and inconsistent local tooling, the solution reads each idea description, applies prompt engineering in watsonx.ai, assigns the request to one or more of eight predefined ISO-aligned categories, and calculates a recommendation using the RICE scoring framework. The workflow then logs prioritization results into the group's roadmap tool so teams can collaborate, track progress, visualize trends, and compare ideas using a shared language rather than isolated spreadsheets and directories. During the six-month pilot, 128 product managers across 10 software products used the approach to reduce manual categorization work and make roadmap decisions faster. The design turns dispersed request data into a repeatable AI pipeline for software planning and portfolio governance.
